overall_summary: Bitcoin slipped below 63,000 dollars today amid heavy tech selling and 114 million dollars in ETF outflows. Roughly 700 million dollars in liquidations added to the downside pressure, leaving crypto markets firmly in the red despite some broader geopolitical relief.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $63,000 amid tech selloff
items.summary: Bitcoin fell under 63,000 dollars as risk assets retreated with tech and chip stocks, tracking a sharp drop in Asian markets like South Korea's Kospi. The move extended a weekly decline of over 3 percent and pulled ether and other majors lower too. Traders should watch how this broad risk-off environment affects crypto correlation with equities and potential further downside tests.
items.impact: Increases selling pressure and volatility for Bitcoin near key support levels.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $114 million net outflow on June 23
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a combined net outflow of about 114 million dollars on June 23 according to flow trackers. This continues a pattern of institutional redemptions seen in recent weeks after earlier inflows. Traders care because sustained ETF outflows can signal reduced institutional demand and add to downward price pressure.
items.impact: Adds to selling pressure and reinforces negative sentiment around institutional flows.

items.title: Bitcoin drop triggers roughly 700 million dollars in liquidations
items.summary: The slide in Bitcoin to the 62,000 dollar area triggered around 700 million dollars worth of leveraged position liquidations over the past day. This has brought the price back to its 200-week moving average and hit related stocks like MicroStrategy to new lows. Traders should monitor liquidation cascades as they can accelerate moves in either direction.
items.impact: Amplifies downside momentum through forced selling of leveraged positions.

items.title: US New Home Sales Data Due Today
items.summary: The Census Bureau is set to release May new home sales figures at 10 a.m. ET. This housing market gauge offers clues on consumer demand and economic momentum amid higher mortgage rates. Traders will watch for signs of strength or weakness that could influence rate expectations and broader risk sentiment.
items.impact: Mild moves in housing-related assets and USD if data surprises.

items.title: Fed Bank Stress Test Results Expected
items.summary: The Federal Reserve will publish its annual bank stress test outcomes today. These results assess major banks' resilience under adverse scenarios and can shape views on financial sector stability. Markets often react to any signals about capital requirements or regulatory tone.
items.impact: Potential volatility in bank stocks and broader equity sentiment.

items.title: DXY Firms as Yields Ease Slightly
items.summary: The dollar index edged higher to around 101.63 while 10-year Treasury yields dipped to about 4.48 percent. Moves come against the backdrop of Fed hawkish signals from last week's meeting and expectations for possible rate hikes later this year. Lower oil prices provided some support to bonds.
items.impact: Supports USD strength which can pressure risk assets like Bitcoin.

items.title: Fed Speakers and Balance Sheet Update
items.summary: Multiple Fed officials including Goolsbee and Williams are scheduled to speak today alongside the weekly balance sheet release. These comments keep policy expectations in focus after the June FOMC hold and new Chair Warsh's hawkish tilt. Any fresh guidance on rates or QT could move markets.
items.impact: Could reinforce or shift near-term rate hike odds affecting yields and DXY.

items.title: US-Iran talks yield roadmap for final peace deal
items.summary: High-level US-Iran talks in Switzerland wrapped up with a roadmap toward a comprehensive deal within 60 days, including sanctions relief and a de-confliction mechanism for Lebanon. Mediators from Pakistan and Qatar called the round successful, though details on nuclear inspections remain disputed. Traders should watch for reduced Middle East risk and lower energy prices supporting risk assets.
items.impact: Eases geopolitical premium, supports risk-on flows and lower oil.

items.title: Dozens of ships transit Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran deal
items.summary: At least 172 vessels have crossed the Strait of Hormuz since the June 17 memorandum, with sharp increases noted over the weekend. Iran and the US dispute ongoing control and potential tolls, but traffic is rising from conflict lows. Lower oil supply concerns are easing, which is positive for global growth and crypto risk appetite.
items.impact: Reduces energy shock risk, bullish for equities and Bitcoin.

items.title: Oil prices fall as Hormuz traffic rises and Iran talks advance
items.summary: Crude has dropped toward $72 per barrel on improved tanker flows through Hormuz and diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran. Markets are pricing in reduced supply disruption risk after months of elevated prices. Lower energy costs ease inflation pressures and support broader financial markets.
items.impact: Cuts input costs and inflation fears, positive for risk assets.

items.title: Conflicting accounts cloud US-Iran nuclear and sanctions talks
items.summary: US and Iranian officials gave differing reports on nuclear inspection commitments and the release of frozen assets in the ongoing talks. Iran described elements of the deal as a US defeat while the US highlighted progress. Persistent uncertainty could keep volatility elevated in energy and risk markets.
items.impact: Maintains some geopolitical premium and price swings.

items.title: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation
items.summary: Keir Starmer stepped down as Labour leader and prime minister amid internal party pressure, triggering a leadership contest likely won by Andy Burnham. He will stay on until a successor is chosen, likely by September. The political transition in a major economy adds a layer of European uncertainty but is not an immediate market driver.
items.impact: Minor near-term volatility expected in UK assets.

items.title: Iran moves to assert control over Strait of Hormuz amid talks
items.summary: Iran has signaled it will manage the Strait under its rules and formed a joint committee with Oman, while the US disputes any re-closure. Shipping data shows mixed results with some stalls over the weekend. Any renewed tensions here could quickly reverse recent oil and risk-asset gains.
items.impact: Risk of renewed supply disruption and higher volatility.
